records.title: Programming 1
records.summary: Introduces C programming, control flow, software design, memory management, and elementary data structures. Provides a foundation for further programming study.

rule.note: Resolve and review enrollment requirement reference 019404 before evaluating eligibility.

records.learning_note: Programming foundations support both directions. Use this to build confidence with C, control flow, and memory before more specialized study.

records.title: Fundamentals of Computer Organization
records.summary: Examines processor organization, instruction sets, memory and caches, and computer-design trade-offs. Uses MIPS and reduced-instruction-set examples to connect software with hardware behavior.

rule.note: Resolve and review enrollment requirement reference 016494 before evaluating eligibility.

records.learning_note: Understanding processor instructions, memory, and caches provides a bridge from programming to embedded hardware.

records.title: Microprocessor Organization
records.summary: Studies microcontrollers and hardware interfaces through C programming, interrupts, timers, serial communication, and analog conversion. Includes laboratories and a project using a microcontroller platform.

rule.note: Resolve and review enrollment requirement reference 016495 before evaluating eligibility.

records.learning_note: Microcontroller programming and hardware interfaces connect an embedded-systems goal with practical device projects. Prepare programming and processor foundations first.

records.title: Introduction to Deep Learning: An Engineering Perspective
records.summary: Introduces neural-network principles, optimization, and engineering applications. Covers perceptrons, convolutional and attention models, and methods for efficient model training and inference.

rule.note: Resolve and review enrollment requirement reference 019593 before evaluating eligibility.

records.learning_note: Neural-network principles and engineering applications connect to an AI/ML goal. Treat this as a later goal until the relevant academic preparation and enrollment requirements are confirmed.

records.title: Introduction to Computer Programming II
records.summary: Develops programming and problem-solving skills through data structures and their implementations. Topics include lists, stacks, queues, trees, searching, sorting, and exceptions.

rule_evidence.reviewed_text: Complete 1 course. C or better is required in CSC 110, ECE 101, ECE 175, or ISTA 130 prior to taking CSC 120.

records.learning_note: Data structures connect introductory programming with the software skills used in later AI work. Check the recorded grade requirement before considering enrollment.

records.title: PyTorch Quickstart
records.summary: Practice a basic deep learning workflow with data loading, neural-network construction, optimization, and saved model parameters. A useful hands-on companion to introductory neural-network coursework.
records.learning_note: Use this to connect Python programming with a small deep learning workflow after building programming foundations.
records.first_activity: Work through loading data and running the example model. Note how the training and evaluation steps differ.

records.title: CS50 — Introduction to Computer Science
records.summary: Build programming foundations through C, algorithms, memory, and data structures, then progress to Python and web topics. OpenCourseWare provides material for independent study.
records.learning_note: Use this alongside programming foundations when you want guided practice outside university coursework.
records.first_activity: Start with the introduction and its first exercise. Move through the material at your own pace.

records.title: AI and machine learning
records.summary: Team learning connection: neural-network coursework and practical PyTorch exercises can support an interest in AI and machine learning. Programming and data-structure foundations provide supporting skills. This is a suggested learning direction, not a hiring or degree guarantee.

records.title: Embedded systems
records.summary: Team learning connection: C programming, processor architecture, microcontrollers, and hardware interfaces form a useful learning direction for embedded systems. A course match indicates relevant study rather than proven job eligibility.

records.title: Introduction to Computer Programming I
records.summary: Programming fundamentals through problem solving, basic control and data structures, and development tools.

children.note: Appropriate math placement requires confirmation; this app does not verify placement scores.

rule_evidence.reviewed_text: Complete 1 course. Appropriate math placement score or C or better in MATH 112 required prior to taking CSC 110. Only one course from CSC 110, ECE 101, ECE 175, and ISTA 130 may be used towards the program.

records.learning_note: Use this as an introductory programming option; confirm program applicability and enrollment separately.
records.first_activity: Write and test a small program that processes a list of measurements.

records.title: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science I
records.summary: Introduces discrete mathematics for computing, including logical statements, proofs, sets, relations, matrices, functions, and modular arithmetic.

children.note: Appropriate math placement requires confirmation; this app does not verify placement scores.

rule_evidence.reviewed_text: Complete 1 course. C or higher in CSC 110 (or ECE 101 or ECE 175 or ISTA 130) and [appropriate math placement or (C or higher in MATH 112) or one course from MATH 113, 116, 120R, 122A, 122B, or 125], prior to taking CSC 144. Only one course from CSC 144, MATH 243 and MATH 323 may be used towards the program.

records.learning_note: Practice discrete reasoning alongside programming; this annotation does not replace the reviewed mathematics and programming conditions.
records.first_activity: Translate a simple program condition into a logical statement and check a truth table.

records.title: Software Development
records.summary: Developing larger software systems with modular design, patterns, documentation, unit tests, version control, build tools, debugging, and performance analysis.

rule_evidence.reviewed_text: Complete 1 course. C or better is required in CSC 120 prior to taking CSC 210.

records.learning_note: Build on programming experience by organizing and testing a project with several modules.
records.first_activity: Split a small program into modules and add a repeatable unit test.

records.title: Programming 2
records.summary: C++ programming with classes and data abstraction, inheritance and polymorphism, exceptions, linked structures, and the complexity of searching, sorting, and traversal algorithms.
records.learning_note: Connect introductory programming to data structures and C++ abstractions; foundation is a preparation label, not first-course eligibility.
records.first_activity: Implement a small stack class and test its empty and nonempty cases.

records.title: Basic Circuits
records.summary: Circuit analysis with laboratory work, covering node and mesh methods, equivalent circuits, operational amplifiers, transient responses, sinusoidal signals, impedance, and simulation.
records.learning_note: Develop circuit-analysis skills before exploring more specialized electronics.
records.first_activity: Solve a small resistor network with node equations and compare the result with a simulation.

records.title: Digital Logic
records.summary: Covers number representations, coding, combinational logic design, sequential systems, and register-transfer descriptions.
records.learning_note: Use logic design to connect programming ideas with digital hardware.
records.first_activity: Draw and check a truth table for a small combinational circuit.

records.title: Applications of Engineering Mathematics
records.summary: Engineering mathematics covering linear systems, vector spaces, eigenvalues, probability distributions, estimation, and confidence intervals, with MATLAB projects.
records.learning_note: Use mathematics exercises to support later work in signals, hardware, and machine learning.
records.first_activity: Compute a matrix projection and summarize the mean and variance of a small dataset.

records.title: Engineering Ethics and Contemporary Issues
records.summary: Introduces professional engineering ethics and contemporary questions about the effects of technology and engineered systems on everyday life.
records.learning_note: Include ethical reasoning when discussing a technical design. The unresolved requirement reference remains separate from descriptive prerequisite wording.
records.first_activity: Compare two design choices by identifying stakeholders, possible harms, and tradeoffs.

records.title: Circuit Theory
records.summary: Analyzes circuits using frequency-domain techniques, Laplace and Fourier methods, convolution, power systems, transformed networks, poles and zeros, and two-port parameters.
records.learning_note: Connect time-domain circuit behavior with transforms and frequency responses.
records.first_activity: Sketch the poles and frequency response of a simple RC circuit.

records.title: Introduction to Communications
records.summary: Communication-system analysis and design using Fourier methods, filtering and spectra, analog and digital modulation, quantization, line coding, and transmitter/receiver concepts.
records.learning_note: Explore how signal representations and modulation choices affect a communication link.
records.first_activity: Compare a message signal with a simple amplitude-modulated waveform.

records.title: Electronic Circuits
records.summary: Studies diodes, bipolar and MOS transistors, operational amplifiers, small-signal amplifier models, digital circuit elements, and circuit simulation.
records.learning_note: Move from linear circuit exercises toward device models and amplifier design.
records.first_activity: Compare a transistor operating point with its small-signal approximation.

records.title: Object-Oriented Software Design
records.summary: Object-oriented design and implementation using classes, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract data types, design architectures, use cases, sequence diagrams, and UML.
records.learning_note: Use software modeling to explain the structure of a larger implementation.
records.first_activity: Draw a class diagram for a small device controller and implement one class.

records.title: The Python Tutorial
records.summary: Official Python language tutorial covering core programming concepts, data structures, modules, and classes. It is written for readers with basic programming knowledge who are new to Python.
records.learning_note: Practice Python after learning general programming basics; this tutorial expects some programming experience.
records.first_activity: Run a short Python script that reads numbers into a list and computes a summary.

records.title: NumPy quickstart
records.summary: Official NumPy quickstart for numerical arrays. Its introductory prerequisites call for some Python knowledge and matplotlib for the examples.
records.learning_note: Use arrays to connect mathematical exercises with Python numerical code after basic Python practice.
records.first_activity: Create a small array and compare element-wise multiplication with matrix multiplication.

records.title: scikit-learn Getting Started
records.summary: Official introduction to scikit-learn workflows for fitting models, preprocessing data, choosing models, and evaluating predictions. The guide assumes basic familiarity with machine-learning practice.
records.learning_note: Practice a simple measured learning workflow after studying basic machine-learning concepts.
records.first_activity: Fit a small example classifier and explain why evaluation uses data separate from fitting.

records.title: Raspberry Pi Pico C/C++ SDK
records.summary: Official Raspberry Pi Pico C/C++ SDK guide describing development tools, example projects, SDK documentation, and initial programs for a microcontroller board.
records.learning_note: Use a small microcontroller project to connect C/C++ programming with device behavior; hardware and toolchain setup are separate practical requirements.
records.first_activity: Read the board-specific setup instructions and trace the supplied LED blink example before adapting it.

records.title: Device Electronics
records.summary: Examines semiconductor electronic properties, charge-carrier transport, junction behavior, and several classes of electronic, microwave, and photonic devices.
records.learning_note: Connect circuit models with semiconductor-device behavior; the preparation label does not resolve enrollment conditions.
records.first_activity: Sketch a qualitative junction diagram and explain the direction of charge-carrier motion.

records.title: Introductory Electromagnetics
records.summary: Introduces electric and magnetic fields, Maxwell equations, wave propagation, transmission lines, and electromagnetic sources.
records.learning_note: Connect circuit and signal exercises with field and wave descriptions before more specialized hardware study.
records.first_activity: Compare the assumptions of a lumped circuit model with a transmission-line model.

records.title: Comparative Programming Languages
records.summary: Compares several high-level programming languages and their characteristics, with programming projects using at least three languages.
records.learning_note: Compare language choices and express the same idea in different programming styles; this is a learning connection, not a prerequisite interpretation.
records.first_activity: Implement a small data-processing task in two languages and compare their type and control-flow conventions.

records.title: MIT 6.006 — Introduction to Algorithms
records.summary: Archived MIT algorithms course covering data structures, problem modeling, algorithmic techniques, and computational performance analysis.
records.learning_note: Archived Spring 2020 material expects Python programming and discrete mathematics. Use it for complementary practice, not university credit or course equivalency.
records.first_activity: Trace a small sorting algorithm and compare its operation count with a second approach.

records.title: MIT 6.004 — Computation Structures
records.summary: Archived MIT digital-systems course connecting transistor-level behavior to logic, sequential circuits, state machines, and computers through hardware/software design examples.
records.learning_note: Archived Spring 2017 material assumes programming concepts and electrical fundamentals; review its syllabus preparation before using the exercises.
records.first_activity: Trace how a logic circuit stores state and relate it to a small processor building block.
